title: The best revenge
hook: the best revenge is not to become like the one who wronged you (Meditations 6.6)

segments.voice: Yesterday: George Long's cold or warm, the duty that doesn't wait for perfect conditions. Did you do one thing well while tired? And today the week closes, so we'll look back too. Day five hundred seventy-four.

Someone cuts you off in traffic, then honks at you. A coworker takes credit in the meeting. A relative says the cutting thing at dinner, the one they always say. And instantly, the reply is ready. Sharper, faster, a little crueler, because they started it. It can feel like justice. Marcus Aurelius was an emperor. He could have answered almost any insult with real force. In book six he writes himself one short sentence about revenge, and it fits on a sticky note.
screen: `THE REPLY IS ALREADY LOADED.` → `AN EMPEROR'S OPTIONS.` → `ONE SENTENCE ON REVENGE.`

segments.voice: First, the sentence. Meditations six, six, in George Long's translation: "The best way of avenging thyself is not to become like the wrong doer." Notice he doesn't say there's no such thing as being wronged. He takes it as given that someone did wrong. The question is what you do next. Second, the trap. When someone is rude and you're rude back, two people have now been rude, and one of them is you. Their behavior has reached inside you and rearranged you. For a Stoic, that's the only real damage they could do. Your money, your reputation, those are outside. Your character is the one thing that's yours, and mirroring them hands it over. Third, why he calls it revenge. Marcus could have said forgive, or rise above it. Instead he uses the word revenge, and keeps it. There's something a little sly in that. He lets the hurt part of you have its wish to win, and then changes what winning means. The wrongdoer wanted you smaller. You stay the size you were. Fourth, the week. Look back at what this week held. How am I using my soul. Heraclitus. Bad breath, where someone's mouth is just their mouth. Soon ashes, and meanwhile, do good. The child's top. Cold or warm. And now this. Nearly every one of those lines is about the same small room: the space between what happens to you and what you become because of it. Marcus keeps returning to that room, because it's the one place nobody else can enter without your permission.
screen: `AVENGE YOURSELF: DON'T BECOME THEM.` · `MIRRORING HANDS THEM YOUR CHARACTER.` · `HE KEEPS THE WORD REVENGE.` · `THIS WEEK: THE SAME SMALL ROOM.` · then, large: `NOT LIKE THEM.`

segments.voice: Sit, and let your breathing even out. Recall one recent moment when someone was rude or unfair to you. Let the scene play, briefly. Notice whether a comeback rises, and where it sits in your body: jaw, chest, hands. Now picture the same scene, and you answering in your own voice instead of theirs. Calm, plain, maybe silent. Not weak. Just not like them. Breathe with that version for the rest of the sit. The bell holds the time.
George Long, whose translation gives Marcus's line: the best way of avenging yourself is not to become like the one who wronged you. Today's word.
Your line: not like them. The next time someone's rude to you today, catch the mirrored reply before it leaves your mouth, and answer in your own voice. Day five hundred seventy-four.

howItsDone: People who draw on Marcus often repeat 'not like them' when someone is rude, as a reminder to answer in their own manner rather than mirroring the other person's.

fork.setup: a coworker takes credit for your work in a meeting. what's the best revenge, by Marcus's line?
options: take credit for theirs next week.
say the true thing plainly, in your own manner, without copying theirs.
fork.reveal: Meditations 6.6: the best way of avenging yourself is not to become like the wrongdoer. Speaking up isn't ruled out; mirroring is.

trapdoor: what you thought: a nice way of saying let it go.
what it means: you were wronged, and the real loss would be letting the wrong reshape your character.
what a scholar hears: Stoics held that only your own choices can harm you, so mirroring the wrongdoer is the one injury the wrongdoer can't do to you without your help.
